description:
Wesam Saad concludes the Tuesday courtship discussion by returning to questions about parental authority and emotional attachment. He says a father’s authority is not removed simply because he is an unbeliever, while distinguishing action within that authority from action outside its proper limits. He clarifies that church involvement may provide counsel, discipleship or respectful conversation, but does not authorise the church to override the father. The discussion then examines emotional purity before courtship. Wesam focuses on romantic longing, fantasy and expectations directed towards someone who may never become a spouse. He urges fathers and young men to protect rather than carelessly awaken those affections.

Using the models introduced earlier, he asks how a person can recognise godly character, respect parental authority and avoid premature attachment. He discusses difficulties with attraction-led relationships, dating websites, visiting unfamiliar churches and relying on a single friend’s recommendation. His criticism includes practical cautions rather than a blanket claim that every approach is sinful. He then describes how cooperation between like-minded churches could provide informed introductions through people who know those involved. Although this is the final Tuesday session, further questions and practical matters during courtship remain unfinished; he offers additional discussion outside the regular study.

questions.question: How does Wesam clarify his earlier comments about an unbelieving father?
questions.answer: He says that being an unbeliever does not by itself remove a father’s authority. He distinguishes unreasonable conduct within a person’s jurisdiction from action outside it. He also corrects a misunderstanding: his earlier mention of church involvement did not mean that the church could override the father’s authority.

questions.question: What forms of help does he envisage from the church?
questions.answer: Wesam mentions counsel, mentoring and discipleship, possibly through a woman designated by the elders, to help a daughter understand her situation and respond faithfully. Where appropriate and with her permission, church leaders might speak respectfully with the father. He distinguishes such assistance from taking over the family’s authority.

questions.question: What does Wesam mean by emotional attachment before courtship?
questions.answer: He focuses on romantic longing, fantasy and imagined married life with a particular person. He argues that purity concerns more than sexual conduct and that these affections should not be carelessly cultivated towards someone who may not become a spouse. His concern is that a person may build hopes around someone who will ultimately marry somebody else.

questions.question: Why does he connect emotional purity with love for a fellow believer?
questions.answer: Wesam warns that repeated romantic encouragement followed by rejection can leave painful emotional wounds. He urges a young man to treat a woman with the care he would show a sister, protecting her rather than arousing expectations while still undecided. He describes guarding such affections as a responsibility of fathers as well.

questions.question: What limits does he identify in dating websites and visiting unfamiliar churches?
questions.answer: He asks how a person can judge genuine godliness from a self-presentation, avoid bypassing a father’s authority and prevent early romantic expectations. Visiting a church may seem more promising than seeking a partner elsewhere, but without existing relationships the visitor and congregation may know little about one another. He presents these as serious practical cautions rather than simply declaring every such visit sinful.

questions.question: Why is a single friend’s recommendation insufficient in his account?
questions.answer: A friend may offer useful knowledge, but Wesam cautions against staking a marriage decision on one person’s judgement, however respected that person is. A recommendation still needs careful corroboration about genuine faith and established character. Seeking that knowledge directly from the woman can also revive the authority and emotional-attachment difficulties he has identified.

questions.question: How could cooperation between like-minded churches help?
questions.answer: Wesam describes known leaders introducing a man through trusted channels to people who have sustained knowledge of a potential spouse. That could allow him to learn from several informed people before raising expectations or approaching the woman directly. He presents such networking as a way to combine introductions with better information and recognised oversight.

questions.question: Does this final Tuesday session complete every planned courtship topic?
questions.answer: It does not. Wesam announces the end of this Tuesday series and the move to Fundamentals of the Faith, but says there is more to discuss, including conduct during courtship and its duration. He offers further discussion at his home. The recording does not supply the promised remaining teaching or establish that those meetings occurred.
